card.name: Digits in blood count thresholds
card.fires_on: A digit inside a large number, such as the first or second digit of 100,000 or 50,000, in platelet or neutrophil count thresholds. It also fires on digits in percentage ranges.

modes.label: Platelet count cutoffs
modes.description: A digit in a number like 100,000 or 50,000 in a platelet or ANC threshold, often per mm3.
modes.example: platelet count of less than <<5>>0,000 cells/mm

modes.label: Dose-adjustment table cells
modes.description: A digit in a table of leukocyte and platelet ranges.

modes.label: Percent range endpoints
modes.description: A digit at the end of a percentage range.

card.writes: It suppresses unit tokens like K, KB and MB, so it steers away from thousand-style abbreviations after a number.
card.plain: It marks digits inside big numbers, mostly platelet or white cell count cutoffs.
evidence: platelet count of less than <<5>>0,000 cells/mm
